answer: What breaks first is the name check. Replay catches duplicates, so a renamed copy dies on its body hash. Divergence above 1 grade point splits the slash between submitter and recruiter, so a failed recruit burns the wallet above it. A mirror of 300 names costs 300 distinct bodies and 300 clean panels, and one slip burns the chain. Cost per fake seat: one body, one panel, one recruiter exposure, no reuse. Nothing about that bill shrinks with volume: a relic of a past answer is worth zero once its hash is on the reject list, and the glacier moves at its own speed.
